chunks: From him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil, from Abu al-Abbas, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

When a man divorces his wife while in his illness, she inherits him as long as he remains in that illness, even if her waiting period expires, unless he recovers. I asked: 'And if the illness prolongs for him?' He said: 'Between him and one year.'

key_terms.مَرَضِهِ: his illness (specifically the illness of death)

ai.seo_question: Does a divorced wife inherit her ex-husband if he dies during his final illness after her waiting period has ended?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the status of the *mutallaqah* (divorced wife) during the husband's final illness, establishing that she retains inheritance rights if he dies before full recovery, even if the *iddah* period has elapsed. The narration introduces a specific temporal limit of one year for prolonged illnesses, a detail subject to scholarly interpretation regarding whether this is a maximum cap or a standard duration for *marad al-mawt*. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on the continuity of marital bonds for inheritance purposes until definitive recovery or death occurs.
